usage: I go to the department store
I buy at the department store
examples: I go to the department store on weekends.
I bought clothes at the department store.
This department store is really big.
nuance: 백화점 is a large multi-floor store selling clothes, cosmetics, and food, usually pricier than a regular 마트.
mistakes: Saying 백화점에서 가요 instead of 백화점에 가요 for going there.

examples: I go to the supermarket in the evening.
I bought vegetables at the supermarket.
nuance: 슈퍼마켓 is a small or medium grocery store for everyday food, often shortened to 슈퍼 in casual speech.
mistakes: Using 슈퍼마켓 for a huge chain store, which is better called a 마트.

examples: I go to the library before exams.
I borrowed a book at the library.
nuance: 도서관 is a public place for reading, studying, and borrowing books, where people are expected to stay quiet.
mistakes: Confusing 도서관 (library) with 서점, which is a bookstore that sells books.

usage: I look around at the museum
examples: I want to go to the museum this weekend.
I saw old objects at the museum.
nuance: 박물관 displays historical objects, relics, and artifacts so visitors can learn about the past and culture.
mistakes: Mixing up 박물관 (history museum) with 미술관, which shows paintings and art.

usage: I go to the art gallery
I view paintings at the gallery
examples: I went to the art gallery with a friend.
You cannot take photos at the gallery.
nuance: 미술관 is a building that shows paintings, sculptures, and other artworks, often holding changing special exhibitions.
mistakes: Calling a 미술관 a 박물관; one shows art and one shows history.

examples: I go to church every Sunday.
I sing songs at the church.
nuance: 교회 is a Christian place of worship where people gather to pray and sing, busiest on Sunday mornings.
mistakes: Using 교회 for a Buddhist temple, which is really a 절.

examples: I went to the temple for the new year.
I prayed quietly at the temple.
nuance: 절 is a Buddhist temple, often built in the mountains, where monks live and visitors come to pray quietly.
mistakes: Confusing 절 the place with 절 meaning a bow; context decides the meaning.

usage: I do business at city hall
examples: I have to go to city hall tomorrow.
I received documents at city hall.
City hall is closed on weekends.
nuance: 시청 is the main city government office that handles public services and official paperwork for residents of a city.
mistakes: Confusing 시청 (city hall) with 주민센터, the smaller local office.

usage: I go to the community center
I apply at the community center
examples: I go to the community center for documents.
I got a certificate at the community center.
The community center is near my house.
nuance: 주민센터 is a small local office for your neighborhood that handles residence reports, certificates, and other paperwork.
mistakes: Going to 시청 for local paperwork that the 주민센터 actually handles.

usage: I go to the police station
I report at the police station
examples: I went to the police station after losing my wallet.
I made a report at the police station.
The police station is close from here.
nuance: 경찰서 is the police office where you report crimes, lost items, or accidents, helpful in an emergency for newcomers.
mistakes: Going to a 경찰서 for a fire; call the 소방서 for fires instead.

usage: they respond from the fire station
examples: I call the fire station if there is a fire.
The fire truck came out of the fire station.
There is a fire station in our neighborhood.
nuance: 소방서 is the fire station where firefighters and fire trucks wait to respond to fires and other emergencies quickly.
mistakes: Calling the 경찰서 for a fire; fires are handled by the 소방서.

examples: I go to the embassy for my passport.
I got a visa at the embassy.
The embassy is open only on weekdays.
nuance: 대사관 is your home country office abroad that helps citizens with passports, visas, and emergencies while overseas.
mistakes: Going to a Korean 시청 for passport help that the 대사관 handles.
